thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: latency_slo.p99 breach detected for /v1/generate (hosted-production). p95 jumped 220ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~ 4.2s over last 6m. Streaming session stalls observed. Auto-page to oncall.

sre-oncall: looking. any customer impact reports yet? :eyes:

raj.sharma: seeing elevated correctable ECC counts on GPU node gpu-7a2 (rack-11). Metric spike started ~ 6789012320. Thermal sensor on that GPU reads 88C and power draw is higher than baseline.

amanda.liu: Confirmed streaming tail stalls: ~12% reconnect rate on streaming sessions hitting that availability zone. Topology: requests routed to dedicated pool-7 which has gpu-7a2 as one of 8 nodes.

dana: oof. Is this a KV cache stall or actual compute throttle? logs show stall loop with repeated kernel requeues.

eng-runtime: grabbing logs. Stack snippet from runtime (trimmed):
```
2026-03-15T17:12:05Z WARN kernel_retry: GpuKernelLaunchRetry count=3 node=gpu-7a2
2026-03-15T17:12:08Z ERROR ecc: correctable_error count=124 window=5m device=gpu-7a2
2026-03-15T17:12:10Z INFO thermal: gpu_temp=88C fan_speed=4200rpm throttle=soft
```

infra-ops: thermal profile shows fan ramps but throttle engages at ~90C. This GPU is hitting soft throttle which increases op latency and causes the streaming tail to pile up.

sre-oncall: can we isolate traffic off gpu-7a2 temporarily and see p99 recover?

eng-runtime: yes — we can live-drain that node. Suggest `kubectl cordon/gpu` + route drain for serving. Will prepare a canary fallback to CPU-backed slot for low-latency customers during drain.

raj.sharma: also seeing ECC correctable errors trending up and occasional uncorrectable spikes (very low absolute) — might indicate hardware degradation. Recommend hardware-ops physical swap after stabilizing traffic.

sre-oncall: okay proceeding with live mitigation. Steps:
1) Mark node as draining in scheduler and remove from serving rotation for pool-7.
2) Reduce batch sizes for pool-7 to avoid long tail while capacity shifts.
3) Route a fraction of traffic to dedicated pool-8 (cold spare) with the same model version.
4) If p99 doesn't recover within 5m, enable CPU fallback for streaming-critical customers.

ops-bot: Executing: `api-router update-route --remove-node gpu-7a2 --pool pool-7` (started)

infra-ops: Starting cordon: `kubectl cordon gpu-7a2` then `kubectl drain gpu-7a2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

amanda.liu: small ask — please keep CS updated for customers on streaming tier. CS, have any customers opened tickets? we might need temporary credits if SLA triggered.

customer-success: we have one high-traffic customer (acme-analytics) reporting timeouts in their ingestion pipeline. We've opened ticket CS-4218 and alerted their TAM. We'll send an incident notice: "We are mitigating a latency issue and routing traffic — expected reduced errors in ~10-15 minutes." :white_check_mark:

eng-runtime: drain in progress. Observed in routing logs: pool-7 active nodes 8 -> 7. Batching throttle reduced to 50% for in-flight requests on pool-7.

sre-oncall: monitoring p95/p99 now. Please paste metrics dashboard link.

eng-runtime: dashboard -> https://console.redwood/prod/dashboards/latency-slo?view=pool-7

(3m later)

eng-runtime: p95 back to 260ms, p99 down to 1.1s. Streaming stall rate dropped from 12% -> 2.3%.

sre-oncall: looks promising. Any errors still on gpu-7a2 after cordon? logs?

raj.sharma: ECC correctable count still rising slowly but at reduced rate — probably because node still finishing inflight kernels. Thermal now 82C and trending down as fan ramp continues. No new uncorrectable errors observed.

infra-ops: recommend we keep node offline for hardware triage. Schedule hot-swap with hardware-ops during next 30min maintenance window. If they want immediate swap, we have spares, but that would incur brief capacity loss.

sre-oncall: decision: keep offline, do hardware replacement during maintenance. For now, confirm performance stable and re-balance.

amanda.liu: CS to send follow-up: "Root cause likely GPU thermal-induced soft throttle causing kernel retries and streaming stalls. We isolated affected node and restored normal performance. Hardware replacement scheduled." I'll draft and post.

customer-success: posted to acme-analytics with ETA timeline. They replied :thumbsup: and asked for postmortem.

eng-runtime: we'll capture runtime traces and kernel retry counters for postmortem. Saving debug snapshot: `s3://redwood-debug/6789012345/gpu-7a2/` (uploaded)

sre-oncall: summary for incident channel:
- Incident start: 6789012320 (detected by alert)
- Impact: p95/p99 breaches; streaming session stalls ~12% for about 9 minutes; one major customer reported timeouts
- Cause: GPU thermal-induced soft-throttle combined with rising ECC correctable errors on gpu-7a2
- Mitigation: drained node from pool-7, rebalanced traffic to pool-8, temporarily reduced batching, CPU fallback available but not needed
- Next steps: hardware-ops replacement scheduled, postmortem doc, add alert for rising ECC correctables + thermal correlation

ops-bot: Incident closed for live mitigation. Monitoring for 1h. :white_check_mark:

raj.sharma: will follow up with hardware-ops and add device to watchlist. Scheduling postmortem tomorrow 11:00 PST.

amanda.liu: thanks team. Good triage and quick live mitigation. :clap:

sre-oncall: closing thread. Marking as resolved for oncall rotation, leave monitor task for infra-ops. "resolved" at 6789012408.
